questions.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=2x-3xy \\ {y}^{′}=-5y+4xy\end{aligned} $$ Consider the Lotka-Volterra model above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators. Select the correct options in the reasoning below. $\,$ Evaluating the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0,\,0]^{T},$ we get
$J({x}^{∗})=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $\,.$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
$\,$ The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are {{field-5}}. $\,$ Therefore, the equilibrium at ${x}^{∗}$ is {{field-6}}{{field-7}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=2x-3xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=-5y+4xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x-3xy)=2-3y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x-3xy)=-3x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-5y+4xy)=4y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-5y+4xy)=-5+4x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J=[\begin{aligned}2-3y & -3x \\ 4y & -5+4x\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
J({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}2-3(0) & -3(0) \\ 4(0) & -5+4(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=2\text{ and }{\lambda }_{2}=-5.$ Since eigenvalues are real with opposite signs, our equilibrium is $\text{an unstable}$ $\text{saddle}.$

$$

Consider the Lotka-Volterra model above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the predators and $y=y(t)$ represents the prey. Find the nonzero equilibrium of the model.

questions.worked_solution:
The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3x+5xy=0 \\ 5y-3xy=0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x+5xy & =0 \\ x(-3+5y) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x=0$ or $y=\frac{3}{5}.$ We consider both cases separately.

- If $x=0,$ substituting it into the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}5y-3(0)y=0\,⇒\,y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, one equilibrium is $(0,0).$

- If $y=\frac{3}{5},$ substituting it into the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}5y-3xy & =0 \\ y(5-3x) & =0 \\ \frac{3}{5}(5-3x) & =0 \\ 5-3x & =0 \\ x & =\frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, another equilibrium is $(\frac{5}{3},\frac{3}{5}).$

Therefore, the nonzero equilibrium of the model is
$(\frac{5}{3},\frac{3}{5}).$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below. $\,$ Evaluating the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0,\,0]^{T},$ we get
$J({x}^{∗})=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $\,.$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
$\,$ The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are {{field-5}}. $\,$ Therefore, the equilibrium at ${x}^{∗}$ is {{field-6}}{{field-7}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=-2x+3xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=4y-5xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2x+3xy)=-2+3y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2x+3xy)=3x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4y-5xy)=-5y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4y-5xy)=4-5x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J=[\begin{aligned}-2+3y & 3x \\ -5y & 4-5x\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
J({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}-2+3(0) & 3(0) \\ -5(0) & 4-5(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-2\text{ and }{\lambda }_{2}=4.$ Since eigenvalues are real with opposite signs, our equilibrium is $\text{an unstable}$ $\text{saddle}.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=ax-bxy \\ {y}^{′}=-cy+dxy\end{aligned}
$$
